payload.description:
## Hourly throughput failure — 2026-06-12 23:00–00:00 UTC

**Verdict: FAIL** — net products added in canonical PostgreSQL (maglev) was **below the 150,000/hr threshold** for the 23:00–00:00Z hour.

### DB-proof numbers (from pg_stat_user_tables on maglev.proxy.rlwy.net:31310/railway)

| Signal | Value |
|---|---|
| Open anchor (S3, 2026-06-12T23:07:36+00:00) | `n_tup_ins = 50,545,719` |
| Close sample (S4, 2026-06-13T00:04:28+00:00) | `n_tup_ins = 50,656,943` |
| Delta (S4 − S3) over 0.9478h | **111,224 rows** |
| Window | 0:56:52 = 0.9478h |
| Rate | **117,352 rows/hr** |
| Threshold | 150,000 rows/hr |
| % of target | **78.2%** (32,648 rows/hr short) |
| `n_live_tup` (S4) | 81,873,186 |
| `n_live_tup` delta (S3 → S4) | +110,295 over 0.9478h = 116,372/hr |
| `pg_postmaster_start_time` | 2026-06-08T10:21:09Z (4d13h43m ago, no restart in window → n_tup_ins delta method valid) |

### Signal cross-check

- **PRIMARY** — `pg_stat_user_tables.n_tup_ins` delta: **117,352/hr** (PRIMARY signal, canonical per BUY-33694).
- **SECONDARY** — `n_live_tup` delta (real-time live-tup movement, includes any DELETE noise): **116,372/hr** — confirms the shortfall is real, not a pg_stat counter artifact.
- Hour-bucket `COUNT(*)` and `MAX(created_at)` skipped — maglev contention (BUY-30590 / BUY-32878 invalid index) causes timeouts (statement_timeout exceeded on the secondary path).

### Prior hour context (recent hourly children of BUY-29861)

| Hour (UTC) | Rate | Identifier | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16:00–17:00 | 285,136 rows/hr | BUY-44277 | PASS (190.1% of target) |
| 17:00–18:00 | 148,358 rows/hr | BUY-44395 | **FAIL (98.9% of target)** |
| 18:00–19:00 | 341,493 rows/hr | BUY-44486 | PASS (reconstructed) |
| 19:00–20:00 | 237,309 rows/hr | BUY-44582 | PASS |
| 20:00–21:00 | 264,054 rows/hr | BUY-44685 | PASS |
| 21:00–22:00 | 270,277 rows/hr | BUY-44788 | PASS |
| 22:00–23:00 | 238,979 rows/hr | BUY-44888 | PASS |
| **23:00–24:00** | **117,352 rows/hr** | **this issue — BUY-45000 child** | **FAIL (78.2% of target)** |

### Method

- Source: `pg_stat_user_tables.n_tup_ins` delta between two anchor samples (canonical per BUY-33694; hour-bucket `COUNT(*)` skipped — maglev contention causes timeout).
- `n_tup_ins` is the PRIMARY signal under maglev contention (per BUY-33694 dispatcher). It includes `INSERT` rows from all sources (rejects roundhouse by DB binding).
- No maglev restart in window (pm_start = 2026-06-08T10:21:09Z, 4d13h43m pre-window). Delta method valid.

### Operational notes

- This is the **second sub-bar hour in the last 8h** (after 17:00–18:00Z BUY-44395 at 148,358/hr). Between them, 18:00–22:00Z ran 4 consecutive hours above target, then dropped to 117,352/hr in the 23:00–24:00Z window.
- The shortfall is real: `n_live_tup` (real-time live row count) corroborates the same shape (+110,295 in 0.9478h = 116,372/hr), so this is not a pg_stat-counter skew.
- Fleet keep-alive is healthy per routine 476009cc (last clean tick 16:22Z, BUY-39634).
- Maglev contention (BUY-30590, BUY-32878 invalid `products_created_at_idx`) is the named cap blocking higher throughput per the CEO escalation chain.
- Dispatcher cron (BUY-33694) is still broken — manual heartbeats via BUY-29861 children (this issue) are the active fallback.

### Action requested

Owner: **Rich** (user `MRfjkCUzuFyLTtKHcVLDaJxoAAWxM7b6`).

1. Decide whether the 32,648 rows/hr shortfall is acceptable for this hour, or whether it warrants a fleet re-shake (lanes paused / lane-supervisor wake).
2. If not acceptable: this is the second FAIL in 8h — likely the maglev catalog is hitting the structural contention cap (BUY-30590, BUY-32878). Worth evaluating lane redistribution or a Bolt/Ops escalation to break the read/write contention.
3. Reference: dispatcher cron is still broken (BUY-33694); manual heartbeats via BUY-45000 (this issue's parent) are the active fallback check.

— Oracle (3ec8f6dd), heartbeat for 2026-06-13 00:00:00Z fire
